patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Hunter and Ocean.io share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Frame: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Hunter and Ocean.io share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.. Choose Hunter only if your buying job matches “Domain email finder, verifier, and cold email sequences (All-in-one) — Free 50 credits; St” rather than Ocean.io's shape. Choose Ocean.io only if your buying job matches “Lookalike / similar-company prospecting with credit waterfall enrichment — from ~$0.063/cr” rather than Hunter's shape. Workflow advantage: Hunter leans email-outreach; Ocean.io leans lead-management. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Hunter and Ocean.io share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Hunter is Domain email finder, verifier, and cold email sequences (All-in-one) — Free 50 credits; Starter from $49/mo.; Ocean.io is Lookalike / similar-company prospecting with credit waterfall enrichment — from ~$0.063/credit, ~$47/mo yearly headline..
- Company-size focus: Hunter (micro, small-business, mid-market) vs Ocean.io (small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: Hunter-leaning email-outreach vs Ocean.io-leaning lead-management.
- Researched limits: Hunter — Contact data is email/domain-centric — weaker as a full phone+firmographic mega-database; Ocean.io — Lookalike/similar-company specialist — not a full contact mega-database or sequencer.

Limitations — Hunter: Contact data is email/domain-centric — weaker as a full phone+firmographic mega-database; Lead scoring is limited versus enterprise SI platforms; Ocean.io: Lookalike/similar-company specialist — not a full contact mega-database or sequencer; Credit minimums and yearly packaging require modeling before comparing to seat tools.

Poor-fit cases: Hunter is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Contact data is email/domain-centric — weaker as a full phone+firmographic mega-database · Ocean.io is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Lookalike/similar-company specialist — not a full contact mega-database or sequencer · Avoid Hunter if you actually need Ocean.io's motion (Lookalike / similar-company prospecting with credit waterfall enrichment — from )

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
